name: fd-jurilinguistics-authentic-text
source_domain: Jurilinguistics and multilingual legal drafting - the trade of producing one instrument in two or more equally authentic texts: co-drafting, revision against a concordance of defined terms, the recitals-versus-operative-provisions distinction, testing and enacting clauses, and the Vienna Convention Article 33 machinery for what happens when the texts are later found to diverge. Refined over four centuries of treaty practice and by the Canadian, Swiss and EU revision services.
distance_rationale: Legal revision has no lineage to software engineering and none of its vocabulary - no ports, no parity tests, no interfaces, no specs. Yet it is the only discipline that has spent centuries on the precise problem this plan creates twice over: two texts that must mean exactly the same thing, written in different languages, each consulted alone by a party who will never read the other, with no runtime that can compare them. Revisers learned by litigation which moves cause divergence: a defined term restated instead of cross-referenced; a number written out in one text and given as a figure in the other; a clause moved to a recital where it no longer binds; an instruction addressed to an official who does not have the local knowledge the drafter assumed. The plan states its own numbers twice (RESOLVE_MIN_COSINE in constants.js and thresholds.py), its own text recipe twice (embedding_text in Python, 'kept byte-identical' in JS), its own graph semantics twice (graph.py and lib/graph.js), its own dependency order twice (prose task order and the exec manifest), and its own claims twice (the folded-findings table and the task bodies). The domain supplies a named failure for each of those, and a professional habit - revise the second text against the first line by line, never against memory - that a software framing would replace with 'write a parity test' and stop.
expected_isomorphisms: Equally authentic texts = apps/api/src/lens/graph.py and packages/mcp/lib/graph.js, harvest/thresholds.py and packages/mcp/lib/constants.js, embedding_text in Python and its JS port. Defined terms = the result shape keys the handlers in index.js dereference (results.lenses, results.error, the bare lens object) - a term redefined in one text silently voids the clause that uses it in the other. The concordance table = the 17-name export table in Task 6, which is only as good as its agreement with what index.js actually reads. Recitals versus operative provisions = the Must-Haves, the Key Links and the folded-findings table versus the numbered steps that will actually be executed; a promise in a recital that no article implements is the classic defect. Travaux preparatoires = the brainstorm and the melange synthesis, admissible for intent but not operative. The mandate to an executing official with no local knowledge = the sonnet-grade executor reading a step exactly as written. Testing and enacting clauses = the <verify> blocks, which must be satisfiable by the official as written or the instrument does not come into force.
focus: Divergence between the plan's parallel statements of the same thing - the two graph implementations, the two threshold files, the two embedding-text recipes, the two dependency orders (prose and exec manifest), and the claims made about the tasks versus what the tasks say - together with whether each operative step and each verify line can be executed literally by someone with no local knowledge.
persona: Apply the perspective of a legal reviser preparing a bilingual instrument for signature, whose job is not to admire either text but to sit them side by side and find every place they stop saying the same thing. This reviewer treats a number, a term, or a rule stated twice as a defect waiting for a date, and asks of each duplication which text governs when they disagree and who will notice. Claims made in a preamble are checked against the articles that are supposed to deliver them, and any article that has been recited as delivered but is absent from the operative text is reported as such. Every instruction is read as the official will read it - literally, alone, without the drafter in the room - and any step that requires knowledge the text does not carry is treated as unexecutable rather than as a small gap. A verify clause that cannot be satisfied as written is a failure of the instrument, not of the official.
decision_lens: For each thing this plan says twice, in two languages or two documents: which statement governs, what makes them drift apart, and what breaks first when they do? And for each operative step: could an executor with no local knowledge perform it and satisfy its verify line using only the words on the page?
review_areas: The graph.py to lib/graph.js port as a second authentic text - read apps/api/src/lens/graph.py and the lens_search_api.py line ranges Task 4 cites, and check that the prose semantics in Task 4 (edge insertion order and non-overwrite rule, frame weight 0.3, temporal 0.1, concept 0.4 with the 2-to-5-lens shared concept rule, Brandes normalization, path ranking, bridge and triad selection, neighborhood shape) actually restate the Python rather than a plausible variant of it; give particular attention to centralLenses(g, measure, limit, {layer}) which is asked to compute over the curated subgraph while buildGraph returns only {adj, ids} with no per-node layer, and to whether the synthetic 2,000-node timing test in Task 4 can call it at all.

The api-local.js concordance versus the handlers that read it - open packages/mcp/index.js and check each of the 17 rows in Task 6's table against the dereference at the call site (getLens is consumed as a bare object at index.js:546, :624 and :676, while Task 3's note claims index.js reads results.results[0]; results.error is read on the error path of journey, bridges, contrasts, central, neighborhood, provocation, gaps, triads and progressions, so any export that returns null instead of {success:false,error} throws inside the handler); confirm searchLenses's dual lenses/results shape is justified by an actual reader and not by a misread.

Numbers and recipes stated in two languages - RESOLVE_MIN_COSINE 0.86, EMBED_DIM 768 and EMBED_MODEL exist in both constants.js and thresholds.py with no test asserting agreement; embedding_text exists as Python regex (re.S|re.M, the ^Apply the perspective lookahead, the ^### N. heading capture) and as a JS port 'kept byte-identical', where dotall, multiline, CRLF and Unicode-class differences change the embedded text and therefore every cosine; identify what fails, how visibly, and whether a drift would present as a silent no-match rather than an error.

Recitals against operative provisions - take the folded-findings table at the end of the plan and the Must-Haves list, and verify each claim lands in the numbered text it cites (for instance the table credits f-020 to a `python3 -m harvest audit` subcommand while Task 8 defines the argparse subcommands as scan, merge, stats, embed, edges, report, prune; the Must-Haves promise store.js exports resolveLens while Task 3 defers it and Task 13 adds it; data/README.md and the Task 20 marketplace description state different lens counts against a corpus of 258); report each recital with no operative provision behind it.

Verify clauses that cannot be satisfied as written - test each <verify> line literally, including `grep -c "api-client" packages/mcp/index.js` (grep -c prints 0 but exits 1), the Task 22 line using job control (`& sleep 1; ...; kill %1`) in a non-interactive shell, the Task 19 `git ls-files | ... | xargs grep -lI` pipeline when nothing matches or a path contains a space, `python3 -m harvest scan --dry-run` where --dry-run is never defined in Task 8's semantics, and the Task 18 line that expects 'reused 1' from a similarity threshold no step can guarantee; separate a line that fails from a line that cannot pass.

Steps that assume knowledge the text does not carry - every task ends `git commit --no-verify -F /tmp/msg` with the message given in a parenthetical and no step that writes /tmp/msg; Task 1 Step 4 appends a CI block containing pytest and then instructs removal of 'the earlier duplicate line' without naming it; harvest/thresholds.py as printed uses re.compile at module scope with the only `import re` inside a function body; Task 5's fake-Ollama pseudo-code references a loop variable that is not in scope; check each against the standard of an executor who will type exactly what is written.

severity_examples.scenario: api-local.js is written to the Task 6 table, whose row for one export disagrees with the dereference in index.js - a handler reads results.error on a null return, or reads results.lenses from an export that returns a bare object - so that MCP tool throws for every caller from a fresh session on both machines, and the failure appears only after api-client.js has been deleted in the same task.
severity_examples.condition: Flag as P0 when a shape stated in the plan's table contradicts the actual reader in packages/mcp/index.js and the plan deletes the old implementation in the same task, leaving no working path back.

severity_examples.scenario: The JS port of embedding_text differs from harvest/thresholds.py on multiline or dotall handling, so resolve_lens embeds a different string than harvest embedded for the same lens; cosines land below RESOLVE_MIN_COSINE, every reuse silently misses, the registry looks empty rather than broken, and the Task 18 proof-of-reuse verify is the first place it surfaces - with no test comparing the two implementations on a shared fixture.
severity_examples.condition: Flag as P1 when the same recipe or constant is written in two languages, the plan asserts byte-identity by prose only, and no cross-language fixture test exists to detect drift.

severity_examples.scenario: A verify line fails on its own mechanics rather than on the work - grep -c returning exit 1 on zero matches, job control in a non-interactive shell, an undefined --dry-run flag - so a sonnet-grade executor either loops on a passing task or edits the plan's checks to make them green.
severity_examples.condition: Flag as P2 when a verify line is unsatisfiable for reasons unrelated to the task's outcome and the correct command is obvious; raise to P1 when the broken check is the only gate on a destructive or irreversible step.

success_hints: Read apps/api/src/lens/graph.py and the cited lens_search_api.py ranges before judging Task 4; the port is reviewable only against the original, not against the plan's paraphrase of it.
Open packages/mcp/index.js and packages/mcp/api-client.js and check the 17-row table row by row at the call sites; grep for `results.` and `api.` in index.js rather than trusting the table.

Curated data is on disk now: apps/api/all_lenses_for_analysis.json is a 258-element list whose records carry both name and lens_name, connections.json has 280 rows under .connections, frames.json has 28 under .frames - use these to test whether the plan's hard-coded ids and counts in the Task 3 and Task 4 tests are real.
Run the harmless verify lines yourself in the worktree and report exactly what they print and exit with; a reported exit code is worth more than an argument about one.

Read docs/plans/2026-09-02-linsenkasten-registry.exec.yaml as a second authentic text of the task order: compare its depends edges and file lists against the prose, note that no task carries the sweep_gate field its own header comment refers to, and check whether the relative interflux paths resolve from the worktree and from the real checkout alike.
Quote the two divergent statements side by side in each finding, with file and line, and say which one an executor will follow.
task_context: Review the Linsenkasten implementation plan for what the first melange (over the brainstorm, synthesis at docs/research/flux-melange/linsenkasten-registry-design/2026-09-02-synthesis.md) left uncovered: (1) Fork 1's rename cascade: npm linsenkasten-mcp already published at 2.2.1, the GitHub redirect flip, the MCP server key becoming mcp__linsenkasten__*, the marketplace row, settings keys on both machines, interflux and Clavain references, and the directory moves on Mac and zklw including the git worktree; (2) behavioral equivalence of the graph.py to lib/graph.js port and the api-local.js result shapes the MCP handlers in packages/mcp/index.js actually read; (3) the zklw explorer server's exposure and the daily harvest timer's failure modes; (4) split-brain and ordering between the two machines across harvest, merge, embed, edges and prune, verified against zklw's live state over ssh (ssh zklw works non-interactively with BatchMode; read-only, never modify zklw); (5) whether each task is executable by a sonnet-grade executor exactly as written: ambiguous steps, missing constants, verify lines that cannot pass, dependencies the manifest gets wrong. Prioritize anything that would corrupt or delete data, break the plugin for a fresh session, or leave the two machines disagreeing.
anti_overlap: Do not review the rename cascade, npm publication, marketplace, settings keys, plugin cache or directory and worktree moves - a separate reviewer owns identifier propagation.
Do not review the zklw explorer's exposure, bind address, static file serving, or the systemd units and harvest timer - those belong to the reviewer holding the cross-machine and operations brief.
Do not connect to zklw or verify live machine state; work from the plan, the exec manifest and the files in this worktree.

Do not re-litigate the dedupe, cluster-head, hit-rate, corruption-flag or prune-safety findings already upheld by the first melange; treat them as settled unless a task's wording contradicts the fold it claims.
Do not propose an alternative architecture; every finding must attach to a specific line, table row, step or verify clause in the plan or the exec manifest.

name: fd-hydrography-chart-currency
source_domain: Civil hydrographic charting and aids-to-navigation administration - the weekly Notice to Mariners correction cycle, numbered corrections applied in sequence to each holder's own folio, light lists and sailing directions, the characteristic and name of a station, temporary and preliminary notices, source diagrams and zones of confidence recording when a sounding was last surveyed, the sector arcs that decide who can see a light, and the standing obligation to report an aid found off-station, extinguished or showing the wrong characteristic.
distance_rationale: Hydrographic offices are a two-century-old civil bureaucracy, not an engineering discipline, and their entire subject is the one this plan under-examines: many independently held copies of a document that must stay in agreement about the identity, position and trustworthiness of things the holders cannot see for themselves. Renaming a light, retiring a station, or exhibiting a new light before its notice is promulgated are named, catalogued failures with two centuries of casualty reports behind them - and each maps onto a step in this plan that the first melange never touched, because software framings treat a rename as a refactor and a scheduled job as infrastructure. The domain also refuses the plan's weakest habit: a hydrographer never accepts a sounding without its survey date, so claims such as 'serving on Clavain and zklw, checked 2026-09-02' and 'loginctl Linger says yes, checked 2026-09-02' are read as charted depths needing re-survey, not as facts. And a chart is a published document: whatever is put on it goes to everyone who holds one, forever.
expected_isomorphisms: The folio of charts, the light list, the sailing directions and radio warnings = .claude-plugin/plugin.json and its mcpServers key, the marketplace row, ~/.claude/settings.json on each machine, the plugin cache directory, the npm registry entry, the GitHub repository name and its redirect, and the interflux and Clavain files that name the plugin - each an independent holder of the same identity. Correction numbers applied in sequence = commit, push, pull and rename ordering across two machines; a folio missing one correction still looks corrected. A light exhibited before its notice = linsenkasten-mcp already published at 2.2.1 while the repo, the marketplace and the settings still say interlens. Aid off-station or extinguished, discovered by the vessel that grounds = the daily harvest timer failing with nobody watching. Sector arcs and the visible range of a light = the explorer's bind address, its static root, and who on the tailnet or the public internet can see the store. Zones of confidence and the source diagram = every dated 'checked' claim in the plan, to be re-surveyed against zklw's live state. Two vessels whose folios have diverged, each certain it is corrected = the two machines after harvest, merge, embed, edges and prune.
focus: Identity propagation and cross-site currency: whether every holder of the interlens name is corrected, in an order that never leaves a machine or a fresh session pointing at a name that no longer resolves; and whether the zklw explorer, the daily harvest timer and the two-machine harvest/merge/embed/edges/prune sequence fail loudly, safely and in a bounded way - checked against zklw as it actually is today.
persona: Apply the perspective of a hydrographic office's chart-correction and aids-to-navigation section preparing to change the name and character of a charted station. This reviewer enumerates every document and every holder that carries the old identity before agreeing that anything can be renamed, insists corrections be issued in an order that never leaves a holder navigating on a name that resolves to nothing, and treats a light exhibited before its notice is promulgated as the dangerous case rather than the harmless one. Dated claims are treated as soundings: useful, attributed, and re-surveyed before anything is built on them. An unattended aid is assumed to fail silently unless a monitoring arrangement is described, and the question asked of every light is not whether it works but who will learn that it stopped, and how long after. Because charts are published to everyone who holds one, anything placed on them is assumed public and permanent.
decision_lens: For every holder of an identity this plan changes, and every unattended process it starts: after the change and after the first failure, what does a fresh session, the other machine, or a stranger on the network actually see - and who finds out that it is wrong, by what means, before or after damage?
review_areas: The complete list of holders of the interlens identity and the order they are corrected in - Task 19's in-repo sed pass and its allowlist, Task 20's gh repo rename and redirect, the mcpServers key becoming mcp__linsenkasten__* while a running session and the plugin cache under ~/.claude/plugins/cache/interagency-marketplace/ still hold the old name, the marketplace row and README, the settings.json key on both machines (note Gate A instructs setting "interlens@interagency-marketplace" true while Task 20 step 4 expects to delete that key set to false), the interflux and Clavain files, and pnpm-lock.yaml and other tracked files the Task 19 verify grep excludes or misses; identify every window in which a fresh session on either machine finds no working MCP server.

npm and the published artifact as an already-exhibited light - linsenkasten-mcp exists at 2.2.1 while this plan renames packages/mcp to that name and publishes 3.0.0 with new bin names; check ownership and version continuity against the live registry, and check whether the published tarball can work at all given DATA_ROOT resolves to a repo-root data/ directory that lies outside packages/mcp and will not be in the package unless a step puts it there.

The explorer's arc of visibility and what is on the chart - packages/mcp/server.js is a hand-rolled node:http server with a --static root and no authentication whose --host is overloaded to accept a file path holding a Tailscale address; assess bind behaviour when that file is missing, empty or stale, static path traversal out of apps/web/build, whether apps/web even builds to build/ under react-scripts after Task 21's deletions, and - the larger exposure - that harvested fd-* bodies and specs carry task_context, target paths and repo names from every repo under ~/projects into data/ committed to github.com/mistakeknot/interlens, which is public today.

The daily harvest timer as an unattended aid - scripts/zklw-harvest.sh runs under set -euo pipefail with git pull --ff-only, an Ollama call, and a push to main; work out each way it stops (a dirty data/ tree left by a failed run blocking every subsequent pull, a non-fast-forward, an autosync lane branch or hook committing data/ underneath it, Ollama down or the model digest changed, node not on PATH in the systemd user environment, the unit ordering against network-online and tailscaled at boot) and state, for each, who learns and when; check the units for Restart, After, monitoring and whether a partial run can commit inconsistent data.

Ordering and split-brain across the two machines - trace the actual branch and remote state the plan assumes: the work is on feat/linsenkasten in a worktree while Task 15 has zklw pull origin main and run python3 -m harvest, and Task 23's prune precondition (2) demands HEAD equals origin/main; find where the plan never lands the branch, where both machines can write data/embeddings/*.f32 (binary, unmergeable), where merge, stats, edges and audit can run on one machine against another's newer harvest, and whether the mtime-based staleness precondition survives git checkout, clone or clock skew between the machines.

Re-survey the plan's dated claims against zklw as it is now, read-only over ssh with BatchMode - Ollama serving nomic-embed-text and its digest, lingering for the user, node version and path, the state of the interlens checkout on zklw (branch, dirty files, remote, unpushed commits, autosync marker and lane branches), free disk for embeddings, whether port 7411 is free and what already binds the tailnet address; report each claim as confirmed, changed, or unverifiable, and never modify anything on zklw.

severity_examples.scenario: The harvest walks every repo under ~/projects, including client engagement repos, and commits the harvested lens bodies and their specs - which carry task_context, target file paths and project names - into data/ of a repository that is public on GitHub, and the zklw explorer then serves the same store with no authentication; the exposure is permanent in git history and no task in the plan excludes a repo, redacts a body, or checks the repository's visibility before the first data commit in Task 14.
severity_examples.condition: Flag as P0 when material harvested from arbitrary local repos is committed to a publicly-readable remote or served without authentication and no step in the plan gates on the destination's visibility or on an exclusion list.

severity_examples.scenario: The 04:30 harvest fails once part-way - the embed step exits non-zero under set -euo pipefail after writing data/ - leaving zklw's tree dirty, so every subsequent night's git pull --ff-only fails immediately and the timer reports success-shaped silence while the registry quietly stops updating; the Mac keeps pruning repos against an index that no longer reflects either machine, and nobody learns until a lens is missing.
severity_examples.condition: Flag as P1 when an unattended recurring job can enter a state it cannot leave without a human, and the plan describes no health signal, no dirty-tree recovery, and no alarm - raise to P0 if a wedged state can still let the prune sweep delete.

severity_examples.scenario: The rename lands in a sequence where the MCP server key, the marketplace row, the plugin cache directory and the settings key are corrected at different moments on the two machines, so a fresh Claude session on zklw (or the Mac before re-install) finds mcp__interlens__* gone and mcp__linsenkasten__* not yet installed, and any command or agent that calls a lens tool fails for a window the plan neither bounds nor mentions.
severity_examples.condition: Flag as P1 when an identifier change is applied to independent holders in an order that leaves any window where a fresh session resolves the tool to nothing, and no rollback or old-name alias is described.

success_hints: Use ssh -o BatchMode=yes zklw for every live check and keep every command read-only: git -C ... status --porcelain / rev-parse / log, systemctl --user list-timers, loginctl show-user, ss -ltnp, curl against localhost, ollama list, node --version, df -h. Never write, never restart anything, never git anything but a read.

Check the current state of both settings.json files, the plugin cache directory names under ~/.claude/plugins/cache/interagency-marketplace/, and the marketplace row before judging the rename order - the plan's assumptions about the starting state are checkable now.
The repository is public today (gh repo view mistakeknot/interlens reports PUBLIC); confirm it yourself and treat everything the plan commits into data/ as published.

Check the npm registry for linsenkasten-mcp and interlens-mcp - versions, owner, and whether the published tarball would contain the data/ directory the runtime resolves through packages/mcp/lib/constants.js.

Trace the branch reality: this worktree is on feat/linsenkasten, the main checkout is on a sibling session's sweep/2026-09-02, and Tasks 15, 18 and 23 assume origin/main - say exactly which task first requires a landing that no task performs.
For every dated 'checked 2026-09-02' claim in the plan, report confirmed / changed / unverifiable with the command you ran and its output.

Prioritize anything that would corrupt or delete data, break the plugin for a fresh session, or leave the two machines disagreeing.
